title: Owner's laws, v2.0 errata (85 entries + 72 row corrections), v3.0 closure matrix, v40 standards/budgets/ADR: constraints the native engine must not violate

items.text: Native only. No VM, JIT or interpreted language inside the simulation.
items.criterion: DO: simulation code is C23 and NASM x86-64 (optionally CUDA/PTX) only. TEST: sim targets are built from .c/.asm sources only; import table of the sim binary contains only the allowed system DLLs; no interpreter or JIT runtime is linked or spawned.

items.text: Cache-resident. Hot loops must not depend on DRAM latency and must never touch a pagefile; state lives in a pre-allocated, page-locked arena; inner loops work on L1-sized blocks of structure-of-arrays data.
items.criterion: DO: one pre-allocated, page-locked arena; SoA columns processed in L1-sized blocks; no allocation after init. TEST: page-fault delta == 0 and allocator-call count == 0 over a 10,000-tick run; block size constant derived from the probed L1d size; lock failure is an explicit error, not a silent fallback.

items.text: No LLM anything. No tokenizer, prompts, APIs, MCP, pretrained weights or datasets; intelligence = genome + development + lifetime plasticity + evolution.
items.criterion: AVOID any tokenizer, pretrained weight file, dataset or network API. TEST: repository scan for weight/dataset files and for socket/HTTP imports in the sim binary returns nothing; all controller parameters are produced from genome + development at run time.

items.text: Zero cosmetic theater. Every mechanism must have a measurable causal effect (a lesion changes outcomes); no hardcoded steering, no label shortcuts.
items.criterion: DO: every mechanism has a lesion switch (data mask, same code path) and a registered lesion test. TEST: for each mechanism, lesion versus size-matched sham on paired seeds changes its declared metric; a mechanism with no detectable effect is removed or marked failing.

items.text: Exact conservation. Matter and energy are integers; totals balance exactly.
items.criterion: DO: matter and energy are integer quanta moved only by debit/credit transfers. TEST: every tick, sum of all pools == initial total + cumulative external input, compared as integers (residual exactly 0); a single-quantum leak mutant is caught.

items.text: Deterministic. Integer / fixed-point state, counter-based RNG (Philox4x32-10); same seed gives the same state hash for any thread count.
items.criterion: DO: integer/fixed-point state, Philox4x32-10 keyed by identity and counter, order-independent parallel reductions, double-buffered state. TEST: same seed and config give the same state hash at 1, 2, 8 and all threads, on P-cores only and E-cores only, at every checkpoint tick; known-answer vectors for the generator.

items.text: Indicator only. Cognition metrics are mechanistic indicators; never claim consciousness or sentience; never call a classical simulation 'quantum randomness' and never claim a quantum speed-up.
items.criterion: AVOID consciousness, sentience, quantum-randomness and quantum-speed-up claims. TEST: phrase lint over source, docs and report output; indicator reports carry the scope disclaimer.

items.text: Honest evidence. Write 'ran' only for what you ran now, with the exact command and the tail of its output; 'unknown' is acceptable, invented is not; no novelty claims without a prior-art search.
items.criterion: DO: every works/compiles/passes claim carries the exact command and output tail; unknowns are written as unknown. TEST: claims register rows without command + output are rejected; novelty claims require a recorded search.

items.text: [Blocker] "Zero observer effect" contradicts level-of-detail switching and the thermal governor. Fix: add one rule and apply it everywhere. Choose one: - (a) level-of-detail and the governor change rendering and telemetry only, never simulation state; or - (b) simulation fidelity is assigned by in-simulation, seed-determined rules, never by camera, inspection or wall-clock time, and is identical [...]
items.criterion: DO: simulation fidelity (LOD tier, substep count, culling, surrogate bodies, sleeping) may depend only on seed + in-simulation state; AVOID any dependence on camera, inspector, viewer attach, wall-clock, frame time, temperature or thread count (owner's v3.0 choice: governor changes rendering/telemetry only). TEST: seed S for T ticks run (a) headless 1 thread, (b) all threads, (c) viewer attached + camera sweep + creature inspected + governor forced through every band: state hash equal at every checkpoint; frame-time-under-burst is a separate gate.

items.text: [Minor] Host-timing senses: recording is specified, but the recorded stream is not a declared input. Fix: extend DIL-06 to host-timing and substrate counters. State that the recorded stream is a declared run input and that canonical Tier-1 runs use a fixed one. Add "recorded" to N90, and say whose hooks N30 means. Replace "GC counters" with a deterministic quantity such as arena water-mark.
items.criterion: AVOID host-derived values (timers, RDTSC, perf counters, thread ids, allocator addresses) in sim state unless supplied as a recorded, declared input stream whose hash is in the run manifest; canonical runs use a fixed stream. Diagnostic probes are read-only (no energy debit). Do not expose a sense that is constant by construction (use arena water-mark, not a GC counter). TEST: symbol/import scan of sim objects finds no time/perf APIs; replay of (seed, stream) gives the same hash; hash with probes on == probes off.

items.text: [Major] "Exact First-Law thermodynamics" is not defined for the soft body. Fix: 1. Define the gate as a ledger invariant and say so in P2. Write "FP64, compensated" in place of "FP64 Exact". If exactness is wanted, hold the ledger as 64-bit integer energy quanta. 2. Make the pool lists agree, and say whether Work is a pool. [...]
items.criterion: DO: conservation is a double-entry ledger in 64-bit integer quanta: every transfer debits one pool and credits another; pools include mechanical (kinetic/elastic) energy or declare it outside the ledger, plus heat and a separately reported numerical-dissipation account. Heat never flows back to a usable pool; a tick that creates energy fails. Tolerances (if any float mirror exists) are relative to cumulative flow, not E0. TEST: every tick sum(pools) == E0 + cumulative external input exactly (integer compare); dissipation and heat accounts monotone non-decreasing; random-transfer property test.

items.text: [Major] "Every part must show a lesion effect" against "behaviour must survive lesions". Fix: state Model 14's reading as the rule: the cosmetic-part test is an acute deficit on a task-specific metric, measured before compensation (or M009's perturbation sweep, in which "every declared organ ... moves behavior"), and robustness is recovery over a stated window. [...]
items.criterion: DO: cosmetic-part test = acute deficit on a task-specific metric measured before compensation; robustness = recovery over a stated window. Declared fixed modules (frozen autonomic weights, fixed random projections) are listed in a manifest and exempt from the no-fixed-helper audit. TEST: per mechanism, lesion at tick t changes the metric over [t, t+W] versus sham on paired seeds; audit fails on any undeclared constant-weight block.

items.text: [Major] Some early gates need parts that exist only in later stages. Fix: define each of the five mutants in one line. Say that Stage 1 runs the mutants against a stub organism (one pool, one sensor, one actuator) and that the mutants and the sweep are re-run at every stage exit. [...]
items.criterion: DO: define the five mutants (Leaky, Cosmetic, Oracle, Frozen, Shuffled) as build or data switches of the native kernel, one line each; Stage 1 runs them on a stub organism (one pool, one sensor, one actuator); mutants and the perturbation sweep re-run at every stage exit; every gate is tagged with the stage whose parts it needs. TEST: mutant target reports 5/5 caught per stage; a gate that references an absent subsystem is a configuration error, never a pass.

items.text: [Minor] Holm status is provisional for items promoted one at a time; "fresh" against "locked" seeds. Fix: state that early locking uses alpha/m, with m the number of tests in the family (the checklist size once C-06's primary contrast is adopted), and that anything else is provisional until the family is complete. State what happens to locked seeds after a failed test (burn the block, draw the next).
items.criterion: DO: early lock only when p <= alpha/m (m = tests in the family, one primary contrast per item); otherwise status is provisional until the family is complete. A held-out seed block is burnt after any failed confirmatory test and the next block is drawn. TEST: harness unit tests on synthetic p-vectors; seed-ledger file marks blocks unused/used/burnt and the batch runner refuses a burnt block.

items.text: [Major] Three release definitions disagree, and some items assume body plans that cannot coexist. Fix: state that GATE-01 to GATE-12 are the release criterion, and that the 825 checks are a scored inventory with a declared applicable set per creature, "not applicable" allowed and recorded in worksheet 10.2. Reword Stage 8 and M100 to match.
items.criterion: DO: release criterion is the fixed gate list; the big checklist is a scored inventory with a declared applicable set per creature/world profile, 'not applicable' allowed and recorded with a reason. Mutually exclusive body plans are separate lineages/profiles, not one genome. TEST: traceability-matrix validator rejects a row with neither a status nor an N/A reason.

items.text: [Minor] N24 "déjà vu on replay" conflicts with exact restore as written. Fix: specify a world-only restore (a repeated-day assay), or a recorded restore channel that is off when M006 is tested.
items.criterion: DO: full snapshot restore is exact; a 'repeated day' assay uses a distinct world-only restore (creature memory kept) or a recorded restore-counter channel that is off during replay gates. TEST: save, run N, restore, run N gives an identical hash stream; world-only restore is a separate API with its own test.

items.text: [Major] The recommended tier cannot pass some gates, and tiers are not comparable. Fix: tag each gate with the tiers it applies to. Fix mesh resolution per experiment, not per machine.
items.criterion: DO: body/mesh resolution and creature definition are fixed per experiment, never per machine or tier; tiers change population count and budget only; every gate is tagged with the population scales it applies to. TEST: the config hash is part of the state hash; the same config on P-cores only, E-cores only and all cores gives the same hash.

items.text: [Minor] Frame-rate requirement is stated in four places with two values. Fix: one frame budget per tier, referenced by HW13 and HW21.
items.criterion: DO: one frame/tick budget per tier, defined once (single header/config) and referenced by every perf gate. TEST: exactly one definition exists; perf gates read it.

items.text: [Minor] Two different "Day-1" sequences. Fix: keep one. The Blueprint's seven-slice minimal organism is the more buildable of the two and is already undated. See also J-01.
items.criterion: N/A-ENGINE: keep one build order (the undated seven-slice minimal organism); the native roadmap uses one sequence.

items.text: [Major] Memory table: the "100 creatures" column is ten times too small in three rows. Fix: correct the three totals (50 GB, 15 GB, 4.8 GB) and the verdict column. The last figure and its verdict are provisional until B-04 is settled: at the 0.59 bytes of the printed layout it is 5.9 GB, and with the two mask bits 8.4 GB. See B-06 for the laptop claim.
items.criterion: DO: every memory figure is computed by a tool from struct layouts x counts, never by hand. TEST: budget tool output (bytes per creature x N) equals the arena's actual allocation; doc tables are generated from it; mismatch fails the build.

items.text: [Minor] Bar label "96 B/syn" does not give 800 GB or 167x. Fix: label the bar 80 B/syn.
items.criterion: N/A-ENGINE: label slip; covered by B-01 (labels derive from the computed figure).

items.text: [Minor] The dense-matrix row describes a different network from the other rows. Fix: state units and density once and compute all five rows for that one network.
items.criterion: DO: any storage comparison states units, synapse count and density once and computes every row for that one network. TEST: comparison table generated by one function with (N, E, density) parameters.

items.text: [Major] "0.48 bytes per synapse" is never derived and leaves out state the spec requires. Fix: print one worked layout per storage class with every field counted (weight, scale, mask bits, delay, index or seed, eligibility), and derive the per-synapse figure from it. State which editing operators are unavailable on procedurally wired blocks.
items.criterion: DO: per-synapse and per-creature byte cost is derived from a printed layout counting every field (weight, scale, structural mask, lesion mask, delay, index or seed, eligibility, runtime state); list which edit operators are unavailable on procedurally wired (seed-generated) blocks. TEST: static_assert(sizeof/offsetof) equals the documented figure; budget tool sums every SoA column including masks and plasticity state.

items.text: [Major] "167x" is measured against a strawman. Fix: quote the ratio against sparse 32-bit storage (about 8-17x), or attach "against one object per synapse" every time 167x appears. Recompute after B-04.
items.criterion: AVOID strawman baselines: every compression or speed ratio names its baseline (e.g. plain 32-bit sparse). TEST: claims register requires a baseline field; benchmark emits both numbers.

items.text: [Major] "100 creatures x 10^8 synapses ... runs on a laptop" contradicts the laptop tier. Fix: retitle Model 8 as a storage comparison for one stated network and drop "runs on a laptop". Add an events-per-second column to the tier table.
items.criterion: AVOID capacity claims ('N creatures x S synapses on this laptop') without a measured run; budget compute (events per second), not only memory. TEST: each capacity row links to a benchmark log with exact command and output tail, labelled 'noisy, parallel load' when applicable.

items.text: [Major] The workstation tier exceeds its own hardware: memory over most of the range, compute across all of it. Fix: cut the tier to what fits, or state that crowd and synapse maxima are alternatives and not simultaneous, and what fraction of the crowd runs a full brain. State the index width.
items.criterion: DO: population and per-creature complexity maxima are stated as a feasible pair (or explicit alternatives) with the index width stated, and must fit the page-locked arena. TEST: arena preflight computes required bytes for the config and refuses to start when it exceeds the locked arena; index type width asserted against max count.

items.text: [Major] "91.4% FLOP savings", "8.6%" and "11.6x faster" are not derived. Fix: delete the three figures, or replace them with "measured: see M005". M005's "≥8x speed-up against single-rate, with stable energy" is the right form because it is a measured gate. If a figure is kept, print the cost split it assumes.
items.criterion: AVOID derived speed-up or FLOP-saving figures; the multi-rate gain is a measured gate against single-rate with conservation intact, with the per-clock cost split printed. TEST: benchmark single-rate vs multi-rate, report per-clock time, ledger residual 0 in both.

items.text: [Minor] The JavaScript example in BUG-04 does not crash at Q = 32. Fix: reword to "silently wraps: Q = 32 allocates two elements". Validate Q as an integer in range before allocating, and compute the size as `2  Q`. The cure (clamp to 10 qubits, 16 KB) is right.
items.criterion: DO: validate every size, count and shift parameter as an in-range integer before allocating; compute sizes in 64-bit with overflow checks (shift >= width is undefined in C, not a wrap). TEST: fuzz config with 0, max, max+1 and shift counts 31/32/63/64: engine returns an error code and never allocates a wrong size; UBSan build clean.

items.text: [Minor] Mock UI numbers contradict the spec. Fix: per-row corrections in the source table.
items.criterion: DO: every displayed or logged number carries unit and basis (relative/absolute, per tick/cumulative, per frame/per tick). TEST: telemetry schema validator requires unit + basis fields.

items.text: [Minor] The governor's bands leave a gap. Fix: make the bands contiguous, express the thresholds as fractions of the tier's frame budget (see A-10), and name the measured quantity.
items.criterion: DO: load bands are contiguous, defined as fractions of the tier budget, and measure simulation step time (not the vsync frame interval); the governor never changes sim state (A-01). TEST: for every t >= 0 exactly one band matches; hysteresis unit test.

items.text: [Minor] Quantities that take different values in different places. Fix: for the first table, one value per quantity, defined once and referenced. For the second, cross-reference the two places or say which is the local limit. Say whether each tolerance is relative or absolute.
items.criterion: DO: each quantity (tolerances, test length, diff size, RNG key fields, tier count, clock dividers, capacity limits) is defined once and referenced, with relative/absolute stated. TEST: constants live in one header from which docs are generated; duplicate-definition lint.

items.text: [Minor] HW06's "under 64 KB" rollback deltas cannot be guaranteed. Fix: use periodic full keyframes plus an input and event log with replay, which the determinism rules already make possible; or scope the 64 KB bound to weight edits.
items.criterion: DO: rollback = periodic full keyframes + input/event log with deterministic replay; a small-delta bound applies only to rarely changing state (weights, masks). TEST: restore keyframe K and replay the log to tick t reproduces the hash at t; delta-size gate scoped to weight edits.

items.text: [Minor] Small label slips. Fix: per-row corrections in the source table.
items.criterion: DO: a block called 'cache-line' is exactly 64 bytes and 64-aligned; a 'tick' always names its clock; bandwidth claims compare against the machine's measured memory bandwidth. TEST: static_assert size and alignment of hot structs; glossary lint for bare 'tick'.

items.text: [Minor] 16.16 fixed point cannot hold the quantities the spec gives it. Fix: use integer time units and a fixed-point format per quantity, and list them in worksheet 10.3. Say in D1 that the ledger is not Q16.16 (64-bit floats with compensated summation, or the integer quanta of A-03).
items.criterion: AVOID one Q16.16 format for everything. DO: integer time units, one documented fixed-point format per quantity with a range/resolution table; dt^2 and slow-decay terms must be representable (use remainder accumulators where one tick changes < 1 LSB); the ledger is 64-bit integer quanta, never Q16.16. TEST: table-driven test per quantity (min step, max value, smallest per-tick delta representable); overflow/saturation counters == 0 in canonical runs.

items.text: [Note] What a 5 ms spike step implies. Fix: per-row corrections in the source table.
items.criterion: DO: any timing-dependent result (spike timing, phase coherence) carries a step-halving convergence check. TEST: run at dt and dt/2; gate metric agrees within the stated tolerance.

items.text: [Note] A real-time budget is never stated. Fix: per-row corrections in the source table.
items.criterion: DO: state whether real time is required and give per-clock, per-tier budgets; the frame-to-tick ratio is handled by an integer accumulator so sim ticks never depend on frame pacing. TEST: N ticks give the same hash at any render frame pacing; per-clock budgets are measured and reported.

items.text: [Major] Holm-Bonferroni is called "FDR". Fix: choose one and use one vocabulary everywhere: "family-wise error rate controlled at 0.05 within each checklist family (Holm-Bonferroni)", with the early-locking rule of A-06. If false-discovery control is really wanted, replace Holm with Benjamini-Hochberg everywhere.
items.criterion: AVOID calling Holm-Bonferroni 'FDR' or 'q-value'; it controls the family-wise error rate. TEST: phrase lint over harness output and docs; column is named p_holm.

items.text: [Major] No significance test is named, and no power calculation exists. Fix: name the test (for a paired design, an exact Wilcoxon signed-rank or paired permutation test on per-seed differences). Add the power calculation, or remove the ledger claim.
items.criterion: DO: name and implement the test exactly: paired sign-flip (permutation) or exact Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-seed differences, integer arithmetic, no normal approximation; include a power calculation. TEST: harness reproduces known exact p-values (16 of 16 agreeing gives 2/2^16 two-sided) and matches an independent implementation.

items.text: [Major] Sixteen seeds give almost no power under the prescribed correction. Fix: set the number of seeds by a power calculation at the effect size you care about, and print it. Two half-measures do not repair the gate. Raising N to 24-32 only removes the smallest-attainable-p floor: at delta 0.33 it still gives under 20% power at the first step in a 500-item family. [...]
items.criterion: DO: seed count N is set by a power calculation at the stated effect size and family size; under-powered = Inconclusive, not pass/fail. The engine must make >= 100 paired seeded headless runs cheap and scriptable. TEST: harness refuses a confirmatory run when the smallest attainable p exceeds alpha/m; power is printed.

items.text: [Minor] The effect size is an independent-groups statistic on a paired design. Fix: state the version ("within-pair dominance, the proportion of seeds on which intact beats the control arm minus the proportion on which it loses"), or drop "paired" from the effect-size clause.
items.criterion: DO: effect size = within-pair dominance (share of pairs where intact beats control minus share where it loses). TEST: unit test on fixed vectors.

items.text: [Minor] "TOST" is the wrong tool for a regression floor, and no margin is given. Fix: use a one-sided non-inferiority test against each locked floor, with the margin preregistered per metric, and add a margin field to worksheet 10.5.
items.criterion: DO: regression floors use a one-sided non-inferiority test with a preregistered margin per metric; AVOID TOST. TEST: harness config requires a margin field; a build that improves never fails the floor.

items.text: [Minor] The number of contrasts per item is undefined. Fix: define the primary contrast per item (for example intact against targeted lesion) and treat the others as descriptive.
items.criterion: DO: exactly one primary contrast per item enters the family m; other arms are descriptive. TEST: preregistration file lists one primary contrast per item id.

items.text: [Minor] Which items need four arms is not stated. Fix: mark each list, or each item, as four-arm, direct-measurement or lineage-comparison.
items.criterion: DO: mark each gate four-arm, direct-measurement or lineage-comparison; conservation, determinism, allocation and performance gates are direct measurement. TEST: matrix column evidence_type is a non-empty enum.

items.text: [Minor] No sham lesion. Fix: add a size-matched sham lesion (the same number of units or synapses removed elsewhere) to the protocol.
items.criterion: DO: lesion protocol includes a size-matched sham (same number of units or synapses removed elsewhere), chosen deterministically from the keyed generator. TEST: sham set has equal count, is disjoint from the target, and is reproducible for the seed.

items.text: [Note] No run budget. Fix: per-row corrections in the source table.
items.criterion: DO: state a run budget (items x arms x seeds, wall time) and share logged runs across items. TEST: plan file computes total runs; measured creature-ticks per second gives the estimate, recorded with the command.

items.text: [Major] The "all 14 must pass" roll-up is not supported by the report it cites. Fix: make F10 a scorecard: report which of the fourteen pass, each with its own lesion control. State that 14 of 14 is this project's engineering target and not evidence of consciousness. Head the column "this framework's operationalisation".
items.criterion: DO: indicator results are a per-indicator scorecard, each with its own lesion control; AVOID any 'all pass means conscious' roll-up or sentience claim. TEST: report generator emits per-indicator rows; phrase lint blocks 'conscious'/'sentient' claims outside the disclaimer.

items.text: [Minor] F2 is named for integrated-information theory but tests something else. Fix: rename F2 "Perturbational complexity (theory-inspired; not a measure of integrated information)". Keep M078's relative scoring, add a synchronised control arm, and apply the pulse to a forked snapshot. Do not borrow the human cutoff (0.31). Update CQM21 and ERR-06 to match. For M078 see also H-09.
items.criterion: DO: perturbational-complexity metrics are named theory-inspired (not integrated information), the pulse is applied to a forked snapshot, a synchronised control arm exists, and no human cutoff is borrowed. Engine needs a cheap fork of a creature/world. TEST: fork, perturb, measure leaves the parent's hash stream identical to an unperturbed run.

items.text: [Minor] Closed-form continuous-time networks: "analytical solution" and "10-50x". Fix: M03: "closed-form approximation; removes the numerical solver. Measure the speed-up in this engine and report it." M02: write the formula with the sub-step factor, for example O(K·E) with K the number of solver sub-steps, the form row M21 prints (K is not defined there either: see K3). [...]
items.criterion: AVOID borrowed speed-up figures; measure in this engine. Closed-form network families are models, not solvers for a given stiff equation. TEST: every speed claim cites a benchmark log.

items.text: [Minor] The spiking liquid time-constant citation is real but needs "up to" and a reference. Fix: "up to 9.2x lower energy than LTC (Vanhalle and Gielen 2025)", with the DOI.
items.criterion: N/A-ENGINE: citation wording ('up to 9.2x', with DOI) only if the paper is cited.

items.text: [Minor] Kenyon-cell sparseness is given as 2%. Fix: at first use, "k-winners 2% code (Kenyon-inspired; measured sparseness is about 5-10%)"; afterwards "2% code".
items.criterion: N/A-ENGINE: if a k-winners code is implemented, call it '2% code (Kenyon-inspired)'; sparsity is a config value, not a biological claim.

items.text: [Minor] Octopus: about two-thirds of all neurons are in the arms, not "two-thirds of motor neurons". Fix: "about three-fifths to two-thirds of the animal's roughly 500 million neurons lie in the arms".
items.criterion: N/A-ENGINE: octopus neuron-count wording.

items.text: [Minor] The antithetic integral motif does not "guarantee" zero error. Fix: "gives zero steady-state error when the closed loop is stable, the set-point is reachable and the controller species are not diluted". Add the actuation equation. In the implementation, debit the same removed amount from both species.
items.criterion: AVOID claiming guaranteed zero error. DO: if an antithetic integral controller is implemented, annihilation debits the same integer amount from both species and the actuation term is present. TEST: ledger shows equal debits; a run with dilution > 0 shows the predicted residual error rather than zero.

items.text: [Minor] The chemoton's third subsystem is a template polymer, not a "GRN template". Fix: box label "heritable template polymer"; split M14.
items.criterion: N/A-ENGINE: name the chemoton's third subsystem 'template polymer', not 'GRN template'; if implemented, three stoichiometrically coupled subsystems with division following membrane growth.

items.text: [Minor] Sleep downscaling is described as global. Fix: "size-proportional downscaling of most synapses during sleep, sparing the largest"; or state that global scaling is a deliberate simplification.
items.criterion: N/A-ENGINE: if sleep downscaling is implemented, either size-proportional sparing the largest synapses or declared as a deliberate simplification.

items.text: [Major] The "quantum" items are classical, and none requires a distribution-matched classical control. Fix: retitle the assay section "Quantum-inspired and geometric interior" and add "classically simulated" to N01-N08 and N50. Require a distribution-matched classical sampler as the control for every such item. [...]
items.criterion: AVOID calling any classically simulated mechanism quantum; label it 'quantum-inspired, classically simulated'. DO: every such mechanism has a distribution-matched classical sampler control and a parameter/compute-matched baseline. TEST: phrase lint; the control arm exists in the experiment registry; no difference is reported except against the matched control.

items.text: [Major] "Symplectic" is misapplied. Fix: "deterministic multi-rate scheduler", "fixed update order", and in BUG-02 "semi-implicit prediction step followed by constraint projection; numerically dissipative overall". [...]
items.criterion: AVOID the word 'symplectic' for the scheduler or the constraint solver. DO: document the multi-rate coupling rule: what is held constant across a slow step, what is accumulated, and the fixed update order inside a base tick. TEST: phrase lint (0 hits outside errata references); the update-order table is a compiled constant with a unit test; cross-clock fluxes use integer accumulators and conserve.

items.text: [Major] "Unconditionally stable" holds only in a narrow sense. Fix: D7 rule and HW11: "integrate the linear decay and leak terms exactly with exponential updates; advance nonlinear terms with a step-size bound that is tested, not assumed". M022: keep "unconditionally stable" only with its meaning attached ("stability does not depend on step size; [...]
items.criterion: DO: exact exponential update only for linear decay/leak with constant coefficients; nonlinear terms advance under a tested step bound; 'unconditionally stable' is used only with its meaning attached. TEST: results repeated at two iteration counts and two time steps agree within tolerance; a stiff-case regression test exists.

items.text: [Major] Most listed number formats do not exist in the stated runtime. Fix: add a note under table 7.1 listing what computes natively in each of the three, and a column "native arithmetic here?" marking the rest "storage encoding, decoded to f32". P14: "optional; needs the device feature; fall back to f32". P16: "no memory saving; native back-ends only".
items.criterion: DO: use only number formats the target computes natively (x86-64 integers, AVX2 integer lanes; no AVX-512 on this CPU); mark anything else 'storage encoding' with its decode cost; probe capabilities (CPUID, GPU) at start-up. TEST: start-up probe result is in the run manifest; missing required ISA gives a clear error; a format table states native-arithmetic yes/no.

items.text: [Minor] "Exact FP64 energy closure" in the GPU tier. Fix: "an energy-closure check computed on the CPU in 64-bit from read-back GPU state, to a stated tolerance". Give ε and the norm. Beyond the horizon where trajectories diverge, compare distributions of outcomes.
items.criterion: DO: on the GPU path conservation is checked on the CPU from read-back state; canonical GPU kernels use integer arithmetic so reduction order cannot change results. TEST: GPU and CPU state hashes are equal for integer kernels; any float GPU path is labelled non-canonical and compared by distribution with a stated tolerance.

items.text: [Major] Bit-identical results across operating systems: the conditions are unstated. Fix: add to the Tier-1 definition and HW15: only exactly rounded operations in the canonical path; the core ships its own versioned fixed-point exp, pow and log, with a golden-vector test on every platform in CI; single-threaded stepping; no relaxed SIMD; [...]
items.criterion: DO: canonical path uses integer operations only (or exactly rounded + - * / sqrt with fixed FP environment); ship versioned fixed-point exp/log/pow with golden vectors; no libm transcendentals, no fast-math, no contraction differences, no host time/random; hashed state is integer; memory preallocated; ISA feature set pinned. TEST: golden vectors pass on every compiler (gcc, clang, MSVC); scalar C, AVX2 and NASM kernels are bit-identical on random inputs; symbol scan finds no exp/pow/log/sin calls in sim objects; hash equal across compilers and thread counts.

items.text: [Minor] Browsers do not "silently fall back" when shared memory is unavailable.
